Hi Mark. In lesson eighteen you learned the long futures, will be doing and will have done, for talking about a moment further ahead. Today we go back to the three everyday ones, and the difficulty is not the form. It is choosing. English has three ways of talking about the future, and they are not interchangeable. The first is will. Use it for a prediction you are making right now, in the moment, with nothing but your opinion behind it. I think they will cancel it. The second is going to. Use it for two things. One, a prediction based on evidence you can point at, like clouds or a trailer or a leak. Two, an intention you already had before this conversation started. I am going to watch it on Friday. And the third is the present continuous, which is the one Brazilian students almost never use for the future, and the one native speakers use most. It is for an arrangement: something fixed, with a time and usually another person involved. We are meeting at seven. Here is the test. Ask yourself whether the plan is only in your head or already in your calendar. In your head is going to. In the calendar is the present continuous. Before class, write three sentences about next weekend, one in each form, and be ready to explain why. See you on Wednesday, Mark.

Right, so the announcement dropped last night and everyone is losing their minds, so let me give you the actual state of things. The teaser is eighty seconds long and it shows almost nothing, which is deliberate. Based on the two frames at the end, I am going to say the sequel is set before the first game, not after it. That is not a fan theory, that is what the architecture in the background tells you. Now for the things that are still speculation. The studio has not confirmed a release window, so anybody telling you it is coming in March is guessing. My own prediction is that they will delay it at least once, because they always do, and because the hype is already too big to risk a bad launch. What I do know is what is in the works, because it was in the job listings: a second team is working on something with the same engine. As for me, I am not staying up for the next stream. I am playing football on Saturday morning and I need to sleep. I will watch the recording on Sunday like a normal person, and I will probably be the last one in the group chat to find out.

First, ask whether you are deciding right now, while you speak. If you are, use will, because that is the form for a prediction or a decision made in the moment. Then, if the answer is no, ask whether you can point at evidence. If you can see the clouds or the trailer or the leak, use going to. After that, ask whether the plan was already in your head before this conversation started, because an old intention is also going to. Next, ask whether it is fixed with a time and usually another person, because an arrangement takes the present continuous. Finally, if two forms still look possible, choose the present continuous, because that is the one you under-use and the one that sounds most natural.
